activities.anchor: Anyone narrating globalisation as an irreversible arrow
activities.caption: scrub the waves — rise, crisis, retreat, redesign
activities.name: globWavesTimeline

events.title: The first great wave
events.text: 1870–1914: the gold standard fixes currencies, steam and telegraph collapse costs, and tens of millions migrate — emigration rates from Italy and Ireland exceed anything in the modern era.

events.title: Crisis and retreat
events.text: War, then tariffs, depression and the collapse of liberal order — the wave pattern established.

events.title: The managed wave
events.text: Bretton Woods: capital controls tolerated, trade liberalised, welfare states cushioning — Rodrik's 'embedded liberalism'.

events.title: The hyperglobalised wave
events.text: Capital mobility, container shipping and the internet — with China's 2001 WTO accession as its emblem.

events.title: The peak
events.text: Trade peaks as a share of world GDP around 2008.

events.title: Slowbalisation
events.text: The 2010s–2020s bring measurable deceleration — finance re-shored, 'friend-shoring' enters the policy vocabulary.

activities.anchor: It seems reasonable — the current wave's vocabulary
activities.caption: true or false — the irreversible arrow
activities.name: globArrowJudge

statements.s: Globalisation is a modern invention that began in the 1990s.
statements.why: The 1870–1914 wave matched today's integration by most metrics — and collapsed in 1914.

statements.s: Integration moves in waves: rise, crisis, retreat, redesign.
statements.why: That pattern is the honest history — 1914, the managed post-1945 redesign, the post-1980 wave, the 2010s deceleration.

statements.s: Trade peaked as a share of world GDP around 2008.
statements.why: Since then: 'slowbalisation' and friend-shoring became policy vocabulary.

statements.s: The post-1945 wave liberalised trade while deliberately taming capital.
statements.why: Bretton Woods tolerated capital controls — the opposite bundle from the post-1980 wave.

activities.anchor: For identity the effects are double
activities.caption: file each concept with its theorist
activities.name: globTheorySort

config.prompt: Three names, three transformations — file each claim:

items.label: time-space compression — distance stops structuring social life
disembedding — relations lifted out of local contexts
money, expertise systems and media carry relations across time-space
the risk society — manufactured risks distributed by interdependence
climate, financial contagion and pandemics do not respect borders

config.why: The identity effects run both ways: hybridisation (Appadurai's five scapes of flow) alongside reactive re-embedding — the local sharpening itself against the global.

activities.anchor: The homogenisation thesis (one world, one consumer culture) predicted poorly
activities.caption: pair each flow with its reversal
activities.name: globCultureMatch

config.prompt: Glocalisation's evidence — pair each form with what it did:

pairs.right: left the Bronx and returned as a hundred local musics
a state-assisted export industry now setting templates for the West
the world's second-largest film industry by volume, with distribution networks of its own
index national taste from Mumbai to Tokyo
survives modified — structural advantages are real, but the one-way street is dead

config.why: Appadurai's deeper point: the five scapes flow at different speeds and directions, and their disjunctures generate the frictions local studies actually document.

config.prompt: What share of humanity are international migrants today?
config.why: 3.6% — about 281 million people, remarkably stable as a share across decades. And remittances to low- and middle-income countries (~$650 billion a year) exceed foreign direct investment and development aid combined: the largest redistributive flow in the world economy — and the most restricted one.
config.context: Capital and goods move under liberalised rules; people under the world's most restrictive regimes.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — the governance ledger
activities.name: globGovSpot

config.prompt: One line of this governance ledger is wrong — click it:
lines: Profit shifting to havens costs governments hundreds of billions annually.
Basel III's capital rules followed the 2008 crisis — regulation follows crisis, not foresight.
The WTO's dispute system was reinforced after 2015 with newly appointed judges.
Paris trades binding targets for universal participation — transparency and ratcheting substitute for enforcement.
Governance deficits are distributional decisions — who bears the externality is chosen by default.
config.correction: The WTO's dispute system is paralysed — its Appellate Body stalled while regional blocs deepened instead.
config.why: The sociological reading: the deficits are distributional decisions by default — which is why the backlash demands they be decided democratically.

activities.anchor: It seems reasonable — capital, goods and data cross borders
activities.caption: true or false — the powerless-state myth
activities.name: globStateJudge

statements.s: States are now powerless — the market decides everything.
statements.why: The lesson's record shows constant rule-redesign: the OECD minimum tax, Basel III, the Paris architecture, border externalisation.

statements.s: The OECD's 15% global minimum corporate tax (agreed 2021) is the first systemic response in a century.
statements.why: Implementing unevenly — but a systemic response all the same.

statements.s: Governance is lagging and uneven, not absent.
statements.why: The correct picture — its deficits are distributional decisions by default.

statements.s: Migration is the flow where states have retained the most real control.
statements.why: Points systems, asylum regimes and border externalisation show it — at rising moral and fiscal cost.

config.prompt: The field's two readings of the world economy — drag the divider:

before.label: The hierarchy reading
before.text: Centres command, edges supply, exchange runs unequal — persistent hierarchy where smoothing was predicted; the 1930s retreat and today's populism are the same dialectic recurring.

after.label: The convergence reading
after.text: Between-country inequality narrowed for the first time in two centuries — population-weighted convergence is the new fact of the world income distribution.

config.why: The measurement disputes sharpen it: unweighted country inequality has not fallen, and household-survey top incomes understate the very top — adjust for tax data and the elephant's trunk grows.
